nodes.label: The Method 1.6 — The Lach Cylinder (book)
nodes.rationale: One claim, demonstrated on one object, with every place the demonstration failed reported.

nodes.label: Lambda - the closed index of atomic transitions
nodes.rationale: A recoding of the quantum numbers adds no physics, so whatever it exhibits is a property of indexing rather than of atoms.

nodes.label: E(X) - external definition cost
nodes.rationale: E(X) = |R(X)| - |X| measures what an index's own coordinates admit and the index denies; openness is a measurement and closure the case where it is zero.

nodes.label: R - the reconstruction/closure operator
nodes.rationale: R recovers value sets and pairwise monotone bounds from a cell set alone, so no outside knowledge enters.

nodes.label: Closed index - a fixed point of R
nodes.rationale: Closure gives six things and no others: alphabet, bounds, totality of the membership test, which cells may be added, which axes adjoined, which constraints imposed.

nodes.label: The periodic table is not a closed index (E = 36)
nodes.rationale: Period and group locate an element but cannot encode why period 1 holds two; that information travels alongside the table.

nodes.label: The void
nodes.rationale: The void is the shadow of the exclusion principle; a tree has no cycles for a sieve to correct, so the count is closed-form.

nodes.label: F - the single expression for Lambda
The occupancy measure
nodes.rationale: Its log is an ordinary l1 metric, which is what converts the additive slack into the multiplicative one.

nodes.label: The constraint graph is a tree (treewidth 1)
nodes.rationale: Every constraint binds one coordinate to one other, so eight nodes and seven edges give treewidth 1; three results follow from that alone.

nodes.label: Rank is conserved - modularity, not submodularity
nodes.rationale: Equality rather than inequality is the signature of distributivity, and it is a cheaper test than checking distributivity directly.

nodes.label: The cylinder - a fibration over the transfer
nodes.rationale: A cylinder and not a Moebius band; fibres are two-body, and it does not factorise and then it does.

nodes.label: The tower - Lambda_9 to Lambda_13
nodes.rationale: The order is fixed as J_c, then K, then J; everything not concerning coupling is stated for Lambda_8.

nodes.label: Lambda_9 and the composition of transitions
nodes.rationale: Transitions compose, and the ninth axis is what lets them.

nodes.label: The clock in the constraint - the occupancy clock
nodes.rationale: The clock is an assumption, and the assumption can be removed.

nodes.label: The decay theorem - why the arrows agree
The electromagnetic index, inside Lambda all along
A.16 - the triangle exclusion, no exact coupling axis
The dichotomy - counting exact, coupling an envelope
nodes.rationale: 2S <= k contains every physical multiplicity and admits values no k electrons can carry; the envelope is forced, not chosen.

nodes.label: The seven constraints and their four origins
nodes.rationale: Exhaustiveness matters because it is the reason the object's properties can be attributed to indexing rather than to physics smuggled in through a bound.

nodes.label: Vector coupling as an envelope (2S <= k)
The cap convention
nodes.rationale: A cap-dependent figure without a stated cap is at the standing caps; what would be a defect is a figure at other caps that does not say so.

nodes.label: Self-reference - alphabet, order, bounds
nodes.rationale: S2, the order, is the hard one; it is recovered only across a tree.

nodes.label: Self-defence - six disjoint defences
nodes.rationale: Three was the count while every defence was built from the object; the other three reach what a term refers to, a coordinate the book does not carry.

nodes.label: D_def - the derivation defence
nodes.rationale: A relation that cannot be violated by data is not empty - it is defending the derivation.

nodes.label: chi_Lambda total - totality catches a missing value
D_ref - a conflated referent
nodes.rationale: Establishing a referent requires reading someone else's theorem and is not runnable by the book.

nodes.label: D_dict - drift from an established referent
nodes.rationale: Maintaining a referent is mechanical once a coordinate carries a stated one; D_ref is paid once, D_dict runs forever after.

nodes.label: D_gro - a term with no referent at all
nodes.rationale: q, the transfer coordinate, has no referent in the spectroscopic literature, so D_ref cannot see it.

nodes.label: Surplus - dim q > dim p
nodes.rationale: Without surplus there is no check; the object found the error because it carried more than it needed.

nodes.label: Extension - E1 cells, E2 axes, E3 constraints
The law of realised closure
nodes.rationale: Restated in certificate form because the first form had no falsifier: ten confirmations and no stated failure mode is what a check must not be.

nodes.label: The realiser as a certificate, not a search result
nodes.rationale: A certificate is checkable where a search is not - one relabelling over 365 cells against 12! refused at that size.

nodes.label: E(X) is the prediction budget
nodes.rationale: An index may be complete or predictive and not both, because a prediction is a proposal about an unlisted cell.

nodes.label: Retrieval as a lattice problem
nodes.rationale: A paywall blocks a source, not a cell; the secondary can be better than the primary.

nodes.label: rho as a property of (document, route)
nodes.rationale: The chapter collapsed the second index; the route is a fibre.

nodes.label: The bracket
nodes.rationale: It uses only measured neighbours, fits nothing and returns an interval - a deduction about where a level cannot fail to be, not a prediction of where it probably is.

nodes.label: A bracket whose admissible set is a singleton
nodes.rationale: The same operation reads as a deduction about a quantity or a uniqueness proof about a kind, depending only on how many admissible cells the interval holds.

nodes.label: The bracket's four rules
nodes.rationale: Each rule is justified by ablation rather than by assertion.

nodes.label: The cost surface V
nodes.rationale: V is a bound, not a tool, and a function of nu/h alone - which makes depth and step interchangeable.

nodes.label: The Rydberg floor V >= 32/11
nodes.rationale: The floor is algebraic before it is physical.

nodes.label: The term function is self-concordant
nodes.rationale: Which explains the cancellation, and names the attribution the book owes.

nodes.label: Domain, failure, and the failure condition
nodes.rationale: A method that has never failed has not been tested; five exclusions are three mechanisms.

nodes.label: The bound in the silence
nodes.rationale: Read backwards, every passing cell is an upper bound on the local perturbation - deductive where a fit's is inferential.

nodes.label: Sc VI 4S-odd - the one deduction, and why it is not a prediction
Collective sections and the assembly rule
nodes.rationale: Error amplifies as the exponent, which is the point rather than a defect.

nodes.label: Aitken's Delta-squared has an exact bias on a Rydberg series
Slack - one quantity, three names
nodes.rationale: All three are admitted against actual; the only difference is whether the comparison is a difference or a ratio.

nodes.label: The register - 1,171 entries
nodes.rationale: Evidence not that the work was error-prone but that the errors were converted into structure; not a confession but the material the method is made of.

nodes.label: Precedent, and what a search can bound
nodes.rationale: Novelty is not the author's to claim; what can be claimed instead is a bounded search.

nodes.label: The documentary language, which has no closure mechanism
nodes.rationale: It carries no algorithm, which is why the precedent question can be bounded and never settled.

nodes.label: Five unlocated results, with the test that would settle each
The reorderability law
nodes.rationale: One statement in two regimes: bijunctive and linear at arity <= 3, containing 1-in-3-SAT and covered by no Schaefer class at arity >= 4.

nodes.label: C1P, monotone endpoints and PQ-trees
nodes.rationale: Correct, and a representation of a 2-colouring rather than the reason d = 2 is easy; strictly is load-bearing in the nesting lemma.

nodes.label: The nucleus - a second index of the same construction
String theory - the pole, the generating function, and a disanalogy
nodes.rationale: Capped coordinates give a finite index and a Sperner bound; uncapped modes give exponential degeneracy and a limiting temperature.

nodes.label: The law applied to this book
nodes.rationale: The book is an index, so the same six mechanisms are run against it, including what a referee would flag.

nodes.label: The cypher analysis
nodes.rationale: A language that falls silent is the finding, and the identity of the silent language names the kind of object.

nodes.label: The six languages and what each can close
nodes.rationale: A language is a coordinate system, and the language a question is posed in bounds whether it can close and at what cost.

nodes.label: The singleton criterion - an index closes when its output class is a singleton
nodes.rationale: R cannot see it: two outputs mean the observer is still choosing which to read, and the choice is not in the object.

nodes.label: Never fit across a language boundary
nodes.rationale: Fitting an integer object is a category error; the constants kept absorbing one another because half the object was a set of surds.

nodes.label: Translation, and what it costs
nodes.rationale: E = 0 is relative to coordinates, and the coordinates must be given.

nodes.label: The Loewdin challenge
nodes.rationale: The target is the ORDER; deriving n+l exactly would mean deriving something false at two elements.

nodes.label: The corridor L(Z) < a < U(Z)
nodes.rationale: One linear inequality per rival, intersecting to an interval; no measurement enters, only Pauli capacity and the node count.

nodes.label: The walk - a carried between elements and reset eighteen times
nodes.rationale: The state is necessary: with no carried value 104 of 106 steps admit two to four self-consistent subshells, so the table is not computable from a single atom.

nodes.label: The entry point t(l) -> sqrt(l(l+1)/2)
nodes.rationale: l(l+1) is the centrifugal term, the only place l enters the radial Schroedinger equation.

nodes.label: Madelung's n+l filling rule
nodes.rationale: A name for the order that is 89% accurate, inverting 5d/4f and 6d/5f.

nodes.label: The four ladders, and the one that reaches the nucleus
nodes.rationale: Z = N_e + c - 1, so no ladder can vary Z alone; the isotopic ladder is orthogonal to the other three and has never been traced.

nodes.label: The principles P1-P23
nodes.rationale: Sorted by what a principle is, they are mechanisms, operations and relations; a relation keeps its content and loses its expression.

nodes.label: The protocols
nodes.rationale: Protocols say how to work with an index; none of them is a theorem.

nodes.label: The grid - the book's method, stated
Triangulation - three results locate a fourth
nodes.rationale: It is a check as well as a method.

nodes.label: The prime directive - nothing runs unbounded
The twenty-five prime audits
nodes.rationale: An audit that reads the wrong artefact will pass anything, so the audits read the object, the source, the artefact and the world.

nodes.label: Audit 7 - ATTRIBUTION
nodes.rationale: It exists because nine things were derived from scratch that were already in print.

nodes.label: Compute, then write - state the number before the interpretation
nodes.rationale: It exists because writing conclusions before reading output was measured rather than deplored.

nodes.label: Redundancy of paths, not redundancy of care
nodes.rationale: Four different things were looking and they were not looking at the same thing; care cannot be increased into a method.

nodes.label: Nothing is something definable
nodes.rationale: A negative result is strongest when the nothing is defined rather than discarded.

nodes.label: Claude (Anthropic) - the collaborator who did the computing
Appendix C - Margins, and what was recomputed
Appendix E - Q, indexed and closed
nodes.rationale: An index states its current contents once, and its history as history.

nodes.label: Appendix F - The numbers, indexed
nodes.rationale: What is not indexed cannot be closed, and what is not closed carries defects no audit is shaped to find.

nodes.label: R applies to ordered coordinates only
nodes.rationale: A monotone bound on an arbitrary ranking of categorical values admits everything above it; the repair is to fibre over the categorical axes.
